title: Keep a placed order as it was placed

blocks.text: Each till has one basket. After an order is placed, the basket is emptied and filled again for the next customer. Billing, packing and the customer's receipt each read the placed order, and one of them once "fixed" an order by adding an item to it.

Finish the constructor of `PlacedOrder` in `src/main/java/practice/Checkout.java`. An order with no items, or with a missing (`null`) item, is refused. Once placed, an order holds exactly the items it was placed with, whatever later happens to the list it came from and whoever reads it. About two lines in total.

cases.says: an order placed from a list holds its number and those items, and counts their units
an order with no items is refused with IllegalArgumentException
an order placed from a basket keeps its items after the basket is emptied and filled for the next customer
a reader that tries to add an item through items() leaves the order unchanged
an order whose list holds a null item is refused with NullPointerException

origin.section: A Method That Keeps Its Argument Keeps the Caller's Object

concepts: An object that stores an argument shares the caller's object, so it copies it on the way in; an unmodifiable view is not a copy, and List.copyOf rejects null elements.
